title: A multiplicative curve character produces an invariant additive character
statement:
Let $U_0/k_0$ be as in
[def-wf-weil-group], put
$\Pi=\pi_1(U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0,\bar u)$, and let
$\chi:W(U_0,\bar u)\to E^\times$
be a continuous group homomorphism, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with its $\ell$-adic topology as in
[def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose
$s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ with $\deg(s)=1$. There are integers
$N,r\geq1$ for which

$$
\lambda:\Pi\longrightarrow E,
\qquad
\lambda(g)=\log(\chi(g)^N),
$$

where $\log$ is the logarithm series of [sk-d-real-log] (so in particular every $\chi(g)^N$, $g\in\Pi$, lies in its domain $1+\ell^2\mathcal O_E$), is a continuous additive character and satisfies

$$
\lambda(sgs^{-1})=\lambda(g)=\lambda(s^{-1}gs)
\qquad(g\in\Pi).
$$

proof.text: Put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$. By [def-galois-fibre-functor], $\Pi$ is the automorphism group of the finite-set-valued fibre functor on a small skeleton, with the evaluation topology. Applying [lem-galois-aut-profinite] to that functor shows that $\Pi$ is profinite, hence compact. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], identify $\Pi$ with $\ker(\deg)$ in $W$. We use the usual Weil-group topology: this subgroup is open and its topology is the profinite topology just described; consequently the restriction of the continuous map $\chi$ to $\Pi$ is continuous.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: geometric group and compactness

proof.text: Use the absolute value of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], choose a uniformizer $\varpi$ and write each $x\in E^\times$ uniquely as $u\varpi^m$, with $u\in\mathcal O_E^\times$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$; define $v_E(x)=m$. Uniqueness gives $v_E(xy)=v_E(x)+v_E(y)$, and the same node gives $|u|_E=1$, so $|x|_E=|\varpi|_E^{v_E(x)}$, where $0<|\varpi|_E<1$. The nonarchimedean inequality of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] makes $v_E$ locally constant: if $|y-x|_E<|x|_E$, then $|y|_E\leq|x|_E$; strict inequality would imply $|x|_E\leq\max(|x-y|_E,|y|_E)<|x|_E$, a contradiction. Thus $|y|_E=|x|_E$ and $v_E(y)=v_E(x)$. These balls are open, so $v_E:E^\times\to\mathbf Z$ is continuous for the discrete topology.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: normalized continuous valuation

proof.text: The fibres of $f=v_E\circ\chi|_\Pi$ form a disjoint open cover of the compact space $\Pi$. A finite subcover therefore shows that $f(\Pi)$ is finite. Since $f$ is a homomorphism, its image is an additive subgroup of $\mathbf Z$. If that subgroup contained $a\neq0$, all integers $na$ for $n\geq0$ would be distinct elements of it, contradicting finiteness. Hence $v_E(\chi(g))=0$ for every $g\in\Pi$. The uniformizer expression in the previous step now has exponent zero, so $\chi(g)\in\mathcal O_E^\times$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite valuation image and unit-valuedness

proof.text: Let $e=v_E(\ell)>0$ and choose $r=2e+1$. Since $\ell\geq2$, we have $r\geq1$ and $r>e/(\ell-1)$. Apply [lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log] with this $r$ to obtain $N\geq1$ such that every $u\in\mathcal O_E^\times$ has $u^N\in1+\mathfrak m_E^r$, together with a continuous homomorphism $L=\log:1+\mathfrak m_E^r\to(\mathfrak m_E^r,+)$. The preceding step applies this conclusion to every $\chi(g)$, uniformly in $g$. The chosen $r$ also has $\mathfrak m_E^r\subseteq\ell^2\mathcal O_E$: the valuation of $x/\ell^2$ is at least $r-2e\geq0$. Thus $1+\mathfrak m_E^r\subseteq1+\ell^2\mathcal O_E$ lies in the domain of the logarithm of [sk-d-real-log], and there the two logarithms are the same series $\sum_{n\geq1}(-1)^{n+1}x^n/n$, so $L$ is the restriction of the statement's $\log$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: choose the deep subgroup and a uniform exponent

proof.text: Define $h:\Pi\to1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ by $h(g)=\chi(g)^N$. Because $E^\times$ is abelian, $h(gg')=\chi(g)^N\chi(g')^N=h(g)h(g')$. Its map to $E^\times$ is continuous, being a finite product of continuous maps, and the map with the subspace codomain $1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ is therefore continuous as well. Compose it with the continuous logarithm and the inclusion $\mathfrak m_E^r\hookrightarrow E$ from [lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log]. This yields the stated continuous map $\lambda(g)=\log(\chi(g)^N)$, and the homomorphism identity of that logarithm gives $\lambda(gg')=\lambda(g)+\lambda(g')$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: continuity and additivity

proof.text: Since $\deg$ is a homomorphism with kernel $\Pi$ by [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], $\deg(sgs^{-1})=1+0-1=0$ and $\deg(s^{-1}gs)=-1+0+1=0$. Both arguments therefore belong to the domain of $\lambda$. As $\chi$ is a homomorphism into the abelian group $E^\times$, $\chi(sgs^{-1})=\chi(s)\chi(g)\chi(s)^{-1}=\chi(g)$ and likewise $\chi(s^{-1}gs)=\chi(g)$. Raising these equalities to $N$ and applying the same logarithm gives $\lambda(sgs^{-1})=\lambda(g)=\lambda(s^{-1}gs)$.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: both conjugation identities and their domains

proof_origin.place: Proof, all three paragraphs; explicit finite-cover and valuation arguments supplied by Q151
